key_insight: CareConnect shows that a tightly scoped LLM agent can automate healthcare scheduling and information retrieval while using deterministic safety guardrails to avoid medical advice and diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce administrative burden and improve access to care by streamlining appointment workflows without replacing clinical decision-making.
method: Built a conversational agent with LLM function calling, retrieval-augmented generation, and layered safety rules.
Orchestrated 8 domain-specific tools for booking, modifying, canceling, and retrieving facility information.
Used deterministic short-circuits to refuse medical intent and detect emergencies.
evidence_signal: In 680 benchmark scenarios, the system achieved 91.8% task completion, 96.0% safety compliance on safety-critical cases, a median latency of 2.2 seconds, and an average cost of $0.0324 per appointment.
watch_item: Performance was reported in a controlled benchmark, so real-world reliability may depend on integration quality, data freshness, and local workflow complexity.
paper_title: Toward Trustworthy Large Language Model Agents in Healthcare
